title: Zurbian (Zurbiyan)
tagline: A saffron-rich, biryani-style rice with yoghurt-marinated meat and potatoes.
intro: Zurbian is the Hejazi and Hadhrami answer to biryani, and a Ramadan favourite across the western Kingdom. Meat is marinated in spiced yoghurt, cooked with potatoes, then layered with saffron rice and fried onions and given a gentle steam. Aromatic, colourful and generous, it sits proudly between the worlds of kabsa and biryani.

items: 1 kg lamb or chicken, on the bone
1 tbsp zurbian or biryani spice mix
1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder
500 g (2½ cups) basmati rice, soaked 30 min
Whole spices: cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, bay leaf
Pinch of saffron in 4 tbsp warm milk
Extra fried onions, coriander and mint

method: Marinate the meat in the yoghurt, ginger–garlic paste and ground spices for at least 1 hour.
In oil, add the tomatoes to the marinated meat with half the fried onions; add a little water, cover and cook until the meat is nearly tender.
Fry the potatoes until golden and add them to the meat for the last 10 minutes.
Parboil the drained rice to 70% in the salted, spiced water; drain.
Layer the rice over the meat and potatoes, scattering fried onions, herbs and saffron milk between the layers.
Cover and steam (dum) on the lowest heat for 20–25 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes and fold gently before serving.
tips: The yoghurt marinade tenderises the meat and gives zurbian its tang — don't rush it.
Parboil the rice to only 70% so it finishes perfectly during the steam.
toServe: Serve with raita or daqoos and a green salad.
